title: FDA De Novo review of Prenosis Sepsis ImmunoScore: AI risk categories track sepsis risk in data from three hospitals
summary: In FDA's review of the Prenosis Sepsis ImmunoScore, sepsis within 24 hours rose from 3.02% in its low risk category to 69.70% in its very high category; AUROC was 0.81.
account: Prenosis of Chicago developed the Sepsis ImmunoScore, machine learning software that uses up to 22 inputs from the electronic health record to place a patient in one of four sepsis risk categories. The validation study used prospectively collected data and blood samples from patients with suspected sepsis at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, the Jesse Brown VA in Chicago and Beaumont in Royal Oak, Michigan. Physicians blinded to the score judged whether each patient had sepsis. FDA reviewers report an area under the ROC curve of 0.81 against the majority judgment, above a goal of 0.75. Sepsis was present in 3.02% of the low risk group and 69.70% of the very high risk group. In-hospital death rose from 0% in the low group to 18.18% in the very high group. FDA granted the De Novo request on 2 April 2024. The study was retrospective, so the score did not guide care, and adjudicators worked at the same hospitals as the patients.
purpose: The Sepsis ImmunoScore was built to identify patients at risk of having or developing sepsis within 24 hours. The measured risk stratification is that purpose.
deployer: Prenosis (retrospective validation on data from three US hospitals)
location: Boston, Massachusetts; Chicago, Illinois; Royal Oak, Michigan, United States

ratings.reason: The risk categories were measured on retrospective data, and no hospital used the score to change care.

ai_role.statement: The study measured the accuracy of the score against physician adjudication. It did not compare care with and without the score.
